reference_drawer.title: 📖 Single-Angle Heights & Distances Reference Guide
reference_drawer.description: Essential relationships for single-angle elevation/depression applications.

items.rule: The angle of elevation is measured upward from the horizontal line of sight.
For level ground, the angle of depression at the top equals the angle of elevation at the observer.
items.example: Transfer the angle to the observer before applying a right-triangle ratio.

items.rule: Original height is the sum of the standing vertical part and the broken sloping part.
items.example: The broken part is a hypotenuse in the resulting right triangle.

items.rule: With inclination θ to the horizontal, the vertical height is opposite and the string is the hypotenuse.

concepts.title: 1. Single Angle of Elevation
concepts.subtitle: Height and horizontal distance form a right triangle
concepts.summary: For an object on level ground, the angle of elevation and the horizontal distance create a right triangle. Tangent is usually the direct ratio for height and ground distance.

points.text: Identify the angle between the horizontal line and the sightline.

concepts.title: 2. Angle of Depression
concepts.subtitle: Transfer the angle to the observer
concepts.summary: The angle of depression is measured from the horizontal at the higher point. For level ground, it equals the corresponding angle of elevation at the observer.

points.text: Draw the horizontal reference at the top.
Transfer the equal angle to the observer's horizontal line.

concepts.title: 3. Broken Tree or Leaning Pole
concepts.subtitle: Add the standing and broken lengths
concepts.summary: The original length of a broken tree is the sum of its standing vertical part and its sloping broken part. The broken part becomes the hypotenuse of a right triangle.

points.text: Separate the standing and broken parts.
Use the angle to determine or verify the sloping part.
Add the two physical tree lengths.

Apply cosine as $\cos 60^\circ=\frac{h}{10}$.

steps.strategy_question: Which move correctly identifies the relevant sides?
strategy_options: Apply sine for the 45° inclination to get $\sin 45^\circ=\frac{14}{L}$.
Apply sine in reverse to get $\sin 45^\circ=\frac{L}{14}$.
Apply tangent to get $\tan 45^\circ=\frac{14}{L}$.
Apply cosine to get $\cos 45^\circ=\frac{14}{L}$.

option_details.text: Apply sine for the 45° inclination to get $\sin 45^\circ=\frac{14}{L}$.
option_details.explanation: Correct! This move matches the right-triangle geometry.

option_details.text: Apply sine in reverse to get $\sin 45^\circ=\frac{L}{14}$.
option_details.explanation: This uses the wrong side or ratio.

option_details.text: Apply tangent to get $\tan 45^\circ=\frac{14}{L}$.
option_details.explanation: This changes the angle relationship or operation.

option_details.text: Apply cosine to get $\cos 45^\circ=\frac{14}{L}$.
option_details.explanation: This skips the required calculation.

steps.hint: Use the angle between the string and the horizontal.

schema_notes.atomic_progression: Every question follows: identify known values and match the appropriate trigonometric ratio → substitute values and set up the algebraic fraction → solve the equation for the unknown side variable → rationalise denominators and evaluate the final distance or height.
schema_notes.strict_options_rule: Every strategy option and option_details text combines a brief trigonometric/algebraic instruction with actual mathematical content; all formulas, ratios, equations and values are wrapped in single dollar signs.
schema_notes.svg_rule: Every pool question contains a mandatory inline responsive SVG using viewBox 0 0 260 180, with the required physical/geometric labels and angle indicators.
schema_notes.latex_compliance: All equations, worked examples and rubric mathematics use multiline aligned LaTeX with at most one equals sign per line.
schema_notes.guided_calculation_compliance: Every step has exactly two vertically stacked outputs and every field uses placeholder Enter value; prompts and field labels do not reveal answers or intermediate expressions.
schema_notes.pool_compliance: Each of the four typologies contains exactly 12 unique questions: 4 Easy, 4 Medium, 4 Hard.
